attempted_claim: Let f: P^2 dasharrow P^2 be a quadratic birational map defined over R whose three complex base points are proper points of P^2 consisting of exactly one real point p0 and one complex-conjugate pair p1, conj(p1), with no three collinear (the one-real-orbit proper configuration), and let f^* act on the Picard-Manin lattice with dynamical degree lambda(f)=lim_n deg(f^n)^{1/n}=spectral radius of f^*. Prove or disprove the growth-gap versus fibration alternative: either lambda(f)=1 and f is conjugate over C to an automorphism of a smooth rational surface preserving a rational fibration, or lambda(f) >= (1+sqrt(5))/2, with the constant (1+sqrt(5))/2 best possible. A complete answer is a proof of the dichotomy for all such f from the 3-point Picard-Manin matrix plus either a sharp extremal example attaining (1+sqrt(5))/2 with certified degree recurrence, or a rigorous counterexample f in this real configuration with 1 < lambda(f) < (1+sqrt(5))/2 with lambda(f) certified as an algebraic integer via an algebraically stable model.
decisive_failure: No proof or disproof of the golden-ratio dichotomy is given. Abstract symmetric orbit data provably admit spectral values in (1,phi), so the matrix-only route is exhausted, and the single explicit real candidate is uncertified because its merged-endpoint orbit map falls outside the standard permutation-type machinery; higher-degree and stability computations were not completed within the pass.
